ModMetaData.name: Wellspring
ModMetaData.author: AzraelGodKing
ModMetaData.description:
Water for the Rim: dig wells, catch the rain, and irrigate your fields.
RimWorld has always skipped the third pillar of frontier life. Homesteads grow food and burn fuel - Wellspring adds the water.
HAND-DUG WELL A stone-lined well with a wooden windlass. Colonists draw jugs of water by hand - slow, honest labor that works anywhere with ground under it.
RAIN BARREL A lidded barrel that slowly collects rainwater and dew. Cheap, passive, and every roofline should have one.
CISTERN A wide, covered stone tank for stockpiling water where the buckets can't spill and the sun can't reach it.
IRRIGATED SOIL Trench water into your fields to work it into rich, dark growing soil (+30% fertility). It can only be laid over ground that could already grow crops - you can't water a stone floor into a farm.
AND MORE A deep well that hauls up 12 water per bill, a solar still that condenses water even in the desert, a 16-stack water tower, a carved stone fountain to show off your surplus, and an irrigated planter box that grows crops anywhere - even indoors. Plus things to make with all that water: boiled water (a humble hot drink), mud bricks (cheap adobe building stuff from water and hay), and clean bandages (70% potency medicine from water and cloth).
RESEARCH Wellcraft (well, rain barrel, cistern, solar still, fountain) leads to irrigation (irrigated soil, planter) and waterworks (deep well, water tower). The first two are neolithic - tribes dig ditches too.
Pairs naturally with Homesteader (water your orchard) and Stormproof (something for the pumps to protect) but requires neither.
Currently fully XML-based: no C# assembly, safe to add to an existing save. Water moves by colonist hauling for now - a fluid pipe system (pipes, powered pumps, sprinklers) is planned for a later release. Before removing the mod, deconstruct its buildings, use up its water, and remove any irrigated soil.
